question.problem:
A tank initially holds $120\,\text{gal}$ of a brine (salt-water) solution containing $20\,\text{lb}$ of salt.
Fresh water is poured into the tank at a rate of $4\,\text{gal/min},$ while the completely mixed brine leaves the tank at a rate of $4\,\text{gal/min}.$
Find an equation for the amount of salt $Q(t),$ in pounds, in the tank $t$ minutes after the fresh water is first added.

$Q(t)=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
Since $Q$ is the amount of salt in the tank at time $t,$ the derivative 

$$
\frac{dQ}{dt}
$$

describes how this amount changes with respect to time $t,$ in minutes. This is equal to the rate at which salt enters the tank minus the rate at which salt leaves the tank.

$$
\frac{dQ}{dt}={Q}_{\text{in}}^{′}-{Q}_{\text{out}}^{′}
$$

Note that the units of $\frac{dQ}{dt},{Q}_{\text{in}}^{′}$ and ${Q}_{\text{out}}^{′}$ are $\text{lb}/\text{min}.$ Now, let's compute the required rates of change in steps.

**Step 1**: Calculating the rate at which salt enters the tank.

First, note that fresh water (i.e., a brine solution containing $0\,\text{lb/gal}$ of salt) enters the tank at a rate of $4\,\text{gal/min}.$ So, the rate at which the *salt* enters the tank is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{Q}_{\text{in}}^{′} & =(0\,\frac{\text{lb}}{\text{gal}})\cdot (4\,\frac{\text{gal}}{\text{min}}) \\  & =(0\,\frac{\text{lb}}{\cancel{\text{gal}}})\cdot (4\,\frac{\cancel{\text{gal}}}{\text{min}}) \\  & =0\,\frac{\text{lb}}{\text{min}}.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 2**: Calculating the rate at which salt exits the tank.

Note that the rate of flow in equals the rate of flow out, so the volume of water in the tank remains $120\,\text{gal}.$
Then, since $Q$ is the amount of salt in the tank, the *concentration* of the brine at time $t$ is

$$
\frac{Q}{120}\,\frac{\text{lb}}{\text{gal}}.
$$

Therefore, as the completely mixed brine leaves at a rate of $4\,\text{gal/min},$ *salt* leaves at a rate of

$$
\begin{aligned}{Q}_{\text{out}}^{′} & =(4\,\frac{\text{gal}}{\text{min}})\cdot (\frac{Q}{120}\,\frac{\text{lb}}{\text{gal}}) \\  & =(4\,\frac{\cancel{\text{gal}}}{\text{min}})\cdot (\frac{Q}{120}\,\frac{\text{lb}}{\cancel{\text{gal}}}) \\  & =\frac{4Q}{120}\,\frac{\text{lb}}{\text{min}} \\  & =\frac{Q}{30}\,\frac{\text{lb}}{\text{min}}.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 3**: Calculate the overall rate of change.

The rate of change equals the rate of entry minus the rate of exit. Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dQ}{dt} & ={Q}_{\text{in}}^{′}-{Q}_{\text{out}}^{′} \\ \frac{dQ}{dt} & =0-\frac{Q}{30} \\ \frac{dQ}{dt} & =-\frac{1}{30}\,Q.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 4**: Integrate the equation.

Separating variables and integrating both sides with respect to $t,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{Q}\cdot \frac{dQ}{dt} & =-\frac{1}{30} \\ \int \frac{1}{Q}\cdot \frac{dQ}{dt}dt & =\int (-\frac{1}{30})\,dt \\ \int \frac{1}{Q}\cdot \,dQ & =-\frac{1}{30}\int \,dt \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡|Q| & =-\frac{t}{30}+C \\ |Q| & ={e}^{-t/30+C} \\ Q(t) & =A{e}^{-t/30},\end{aligned}
$$

where $A=\pm {e}^{C}$ is a constant of integration.

We're told that the tank initially contains $20\,\text{lb}$ of salt. So, we can apply the initial condition $Q(0)=20,$ and solve for $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(0) & =20 \\ A{e}^{-0/30} & =20 \\ A & =20\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain the following expression for $Q(t):$

$$
Q(t)=20{e}^{-t/30}
$$
